Behavior Tree region — Detach and identity

Two bugs, one seam. Detach to primitives on a Behavior Tree region threw ValidationError and unmounted the whole React app; duplicating or pasting a region scrambled the layout of the region it was copied from. The first was a value that is legal in a shape's props and illegal in its meta; the second was a stored id trusted after copy and paste re-minted every id around it. Both are fixed at the seam that owns the invariant, both have a real-browser journey that can go red, and the region now lowers whole to stock tldraw. Built on main at b2ac9670 (uncommitted), tldraw 5.3.2, 2026-09-05.

1 · Detach crashed the app

Symptom. Right-click the region's header band, choose Detach to primitives: ValidationError: At shape(type = group).meta: Expected json serializable value, got object, and the app is gone — window.__systemsketch disappears, the canvas unmounts.

Reproduction, measured against the running app before the fix

SelectionOutcomeCrashXML afterLeft behind

Two different failures in one table. The region crashes. A projected child "succeeds" — and the XML shrinks, because detaching a projected occurrence was never a legitimate operation: its truth is the region's XML, and deleting the Block record compiles an XML delete. Asking to detach a node silently removed it from the tree.

Root cause — one value, two validators

  1. src/blocks/definitions/definitionLinking.ts:539 passes draftOrdinal: canonical.props.draftOrdinal — an absent optional prop, so the value is undefined — into updateDefinitionGroup (line 384), which spreads it into props (line 393).
  2. tldraw's applyPartialToRecordWithProps (@tldraw/editor/dist-esm/lib/editor/Editor.mjs:8735–8758) skips a top-level undefined in a partial (line 8741) but copies every props/meta sub-key verbatim (lines 8745–8750). The store record now literally holds draftOrdinal: undefined.
  3. That is legal for props — draftOrdinal: T.number.optional(), src/blocks/blockModel.ts:349 — and illegal for meta: createShapeValidator (@tldraw/tlschema/dist-esm/shapes/TLBaseShape.mjs:24) validates meta with T.jsonValue, whose isValidJson (@tldraw/validate/dist-esm/lib/validation.mjs:857–878) rejects undefined anywhere in the tree.
  4. src/blocks/detach/detachBlock.ts:226 copies the whole block.props into the detached group's meta. Crash.
  5. Why the message was hard to read. It says got object and points at .meta, not at draftOrdinal, because jsonValue is a leaf validator with no path tracking: isValidJson returns a bare false from wherever it fails and the error is composed at the top with typeof value of the whole meta. The offending key is never named.
  6. Why the Behavior Tree region specifically. The sample tree repeats leaf names (CloseGrip ×3, MoveHome ×3). The duplicate-title reconciler at definitionLinking.ts:535–540 fires for the content-identical copies, so exactly 4 of the 9 projected Blocks (paths 0.4.0, 0.4.1.0, 0.4.1.1, 0.4.2) carried draftOrdinal: undefined. Detaching one clean leaf worked; detaching the region swept all nine and hit a poisoned one. Proved by monkey-patching editor.store.put in the live page and capturing the stack of the write that planted it: updateDefinitionGroup (definitionLinking.ts) ← reconcileExistingDefinitionNames.

The fix, at the seam that owns the invariant

A new exported toJsonSafe in src/blocks/detach/detachModel.ts deep-copies a value dropping present-but-undefined keys; an array hole becomes null, which is what JSON would do. detachMeta runs every record through it, and detachBranch.ts / detachLoop.ts do too — they had the same latent crash via structuredClone(props).

Deliberately not "fixed" upstream. Writing draftOrdinal: undefined is the only way tldraw's update merge can express cleared; dropping the key from the patch would keep the OLD value and a set ordinal would stop being clearable. definitionLinking.ts gets a WHY: comment saying so and nothing else:

The region detaches whole

New src/behaviorTree/detachBehaviorTree.ts plus a pure src/behaviorTree/btPrimitives.ts. The region becomes a stock frame named for the tree, carrying the canonical BT.CPP XML in JSON-only meta; each projected leaf and pill goes through the ordinary Block detach and becomes the same stock group any detached Block becomes; Dataflow cables go through the ordinary connection detach; and the layer the region paints for itself — control cards, wires, rails, merge marks, chips, group boxes, Start — becomes stock line / geo / text records. Wired into detachSelectedPrimitives and into src/export/portableTldraw.ts beside Branch and Loop, with tests/test_stock_boundary.py extended to require it.

The export UI reported “Downloaded a stock-tldraw copy. Your live board was not changed.” with no console errors. Before this change portableTldraw.ts did not register BehaviorTreeShapeUtil or BtControlShapeUtil at all, so a board containing a region could not even be loaded into the isolated export store, let alone lowered.

2 · Duplicating or pasting a region scrambled the original

Zach recorded it. Row store-000325 of /home/bam/systemsketch/docs/assets/behavior-tree-identity/recording-store-000325.json is the Ctrl+V, at t = 10637.5 ms, source user: 18 records added (a second behaviorTree and its projection) and 43 updated. Among the updated records is the original region shape:vDWuwUTulofT4T6da223D, whose props.offsets goes from {} to 12 entries, the largest 14,495 px — 13.5× the region's own width. That is the distance to the pasted copies, recorded as if someone had dragged each original card there. Tidy clears offsets, which is why Tidy appeared to repair it. The pasted control cards in the same row arrive stamped shape:subject ×5 — a region id that exists nowhere on the board: the stamp is whatever the copied shape had.

Root cause — a stored id, trusted after every id was re-minted

src/behaviorTree/installBehaviorTreeRegions.ts resolved a projected child's region from meta.btRegion, a stored id. tldraw re-mints every shape id on duplicate and paste but copies meta verbatim, so a copied child still names the region it was copied from. Every rule that read that name then acted on the original: reparent the copy into it, record the paste distance as one of its free offsets, and delete its own children as duplicate role:path strays.

The fix — containment decides

New behaviorTreeRegionFor / behaviorTreeRegionAncestor resolve a child's region by walking up to the nearest region ancestor; a cable — parented at page level by the connection layer — resolves through its bindings' Blocks. The stored id survives only as the fallback for the one case containment cannot answer: a child dragged clean out of every region, which the drag rule then pulls back. A second, independent guard: the set of shapes created in the current operation, so a freshly-created arrival is never read as a drag — that is what wrote the huge offsets. And reconcileBehaviorTree re-stamps a copied child's btRegion so a later delete edits the right tree's XML.

Decision surface

Done and proved

  • Detach on a region no longer crashes; it lowers the region to one stock frame of stock records, undoes in one step, and stock tldraw 5.3.2 with no SystemSketch utilities renders the result — 26/26 in a real browser, plus the exported .tldr measured above.
  • A projected child is refused, not lowered: the menu item does not appear and the XML is byte-identical.
  • The latent structuredClone(props) crash in Branch and Loop detach is closed by the same toJsonSafe.
  • Duplicate, paste, move and the Dataflow lens leave the original region's offsets and children untouched — 33/33, and 12 of those go red when the fix is mutated out.
  • The identity rule has a decision record. docs/peps/0004-projected-child-ownership-by-containment.md — A projected child's owning region is derived from containment, not from a stored id — records why the stored stamp is kept and repaired rather than deleted, linked from the WHY: at behaviorTreeRegionFor. tests/test_pep_links.py fails if that pointer ever rots.

Left, and not blocked

  • Importing a detached frame back into a region (the frame carries the XML for exactly that; no reader exists yet).
  • package.json scripts for the two new journeys — another agent holds that file; run them by path until then.

Needs Zach

  • Merge. Everything is on main in the primary checkout and nothing is pushed — the remote moves only when you say so. (This report is inside the commit it describes, so its header stamps the tree as it stood at build time.)

Deliberately not done

  • Not "fixing" definitionLinking.ts to delete the key: undefined in the patch is the only spelling of cleared tldraw's merge understands.
  • Not lowering a projected child on its own, ever: its truth is the XML, and the primitives would claim to be an authored Block.
  • Not a stock arrow for control wires: an elbow cannot be an arrow, so the head is its own triangle and the wire stays a faithful polyline.
  • Not touching treeLayout.ts, layouts.test.ts, behavior_tree_smoke.mjs or package.json: other agents are in them.
